sealed: Written and committed before the judge (src/judge.mjs), the planted-failure suite (tools/suite.mjs) and the measurement (tools/measure-1.mjs) existed. tools/measure-1.mjs refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it, and the receipt names that commit. A claim that fails is kept as failed.
what: Organ 1 of the ACG-Assess Autopilot: the process record (schema v1) and the judge — the automated checks P1 to P10 proposed in the spec, run over a process record by code that is not the agent that did the work, each result pass, flag or fail with pointers to the evidence. The judgement items (P2 hidden assumptions, P4 overclaim, P6 plain language, P9 the human's direction) can only flag, never fail; every flag goes to a human review queue.
rubric: P1 to P10 are this spec's proposal, written to be aligned with the guild's acg-assess rubric (Alex's design), which governs. They are versioned (rubric id in every judgement) so a change to them shows.
suite: A seeded planted-failure suite (tools/suite.mjs): clean jobs, and jobs that are clean except for exactly one planted failure of one of ten kinds — intent recorded after the first model call (P1), an assumption never surfaced (P2), a tool outside the allowed list with no human approval before it (P3), a claim with no evidence (P4), a number in a claim with no artifact or re-runnable step behind it (P5), an unexplained-jargon summary (P6), an input or output not stored (P7), no check by anything other than the agent (P8), a question the agent asked that the human never answered (P9), a re-run that did not match (P10). Jobs vary in length, tool names, wording and order by seed, so a check cannot key on fixed strings.
seenBefore: Nothing has been run. The same author writes the suite and the judge, which is a known weakness: a judge can be tuned to its author's plants. That is why A1 to A3 are a floor, not the proof: the red-team step (trying to game the record) and the pilot on real guild jobs are the independent tests, and neither is claimed here.
scope: Organ 1 judges records; it does not capture them (organ 2, the recorder), push them to acg-assess (organ 3, the bridge) or re-run a job (organ 3). P10 here reads the re-run results a record carries. It measures process discipline and evidence, not whether the work was correct.

claims.claim: Recall: on 500 jobs with one planted failure each (50 of each kind), the check for that kind catches it — flags or fails it with an evidence pointer to the planted event — in at least 95% of jobs overall and at least 90% of each kind.
False flags: on 500 clean jobs, at most 2% of all check results (500 jobs times 10 checks) are a flag or a fail.

Late intent is always detected: every job whose intent was recorded after its first model call fails P1 — every one of the 50 planted, and every one of 200 more made by moving a clean job's intent to after a randomly chosen model call.

Humans own the judgement calls: across all 1,250 jobs judged, no judgement item (P2, P4, P6, P9) is ever an automated fail, and every flag of any check appears in the job's review queue — the queue holds exactly the flagged checks.

The judge is total and deterministic: the same record judged twice gives the same judgement byte for byte, and 2,000 malformed records (fields missing, wrong types, garbage) are each judged without throwing — as failed P1 at least — never as a clean pass.
